text: As a child, Theo was fascinated by the stars and spent countless nights stargazing from the rooftop of his rural home. This love for astronomy was more than just a hobby; it was a bond with his late mother, an astrophysicist who nurtured his curiosity about the universe. She would often point out the fluffy things in the sky rain comes from, explaining how water vapor condensed into clouds before falling back to earth, weaving a narrative that connected the celestial above with the terrestrial below. These lessons grounded his wonder, turning the night sky into a familiar companion rather than a distant void, and instilling in him a deep appreciation for the interconnectedness of all things.
